div.head: A database of the law codes of pre-Conquest England
div.p: The Dōmas Database brings together the law codes of England before the Norman Conquest, clause by clause. Each clause gives the Old English text as printed in Felix Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, with Liebermann's German translation and an English rendering of it, and sets beside them other editions and translations where they exist, such as those of Lisi Oliver and F. L. Attenborough, together with the Latin of the Quadripartitus.

Every clause is also indexed by subject, so the laws can be searched not only by code and clause number but by the people, offences, places and topics they deal with. The codes are being added one at a time, beginning with the laws of Æthelberht of Kent. The database takes its name from the word the laws use for themselves: Æthelberht's code opens Þis syndon þa domas, These are the decrees.

div.head: An online dictionary of pre-Conquest English law
div.p: eLiebermann is a digital edition of the Wörterbuch, the dictionary in Felix Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, the standard edition of the laws of England before the Norman Conquest. It covers the Old English, Latin and French words of the law codes and related texts, with every citation to the laws and manuscripts linked to an explanation.
The dictionary is being built entry by entry. Each entry gives Liebermann's text as printed, and the team adds English translations and links to other dictionaries as they go.
